verdict.rationale: Gmail natively provides filters, which are rules that evaluate incoming mail against criteria such as sender, subject or size and then automatically label or forward matching messages in the background. That is a real autonomous automation, but it is limited to fixed rule-based actions. Gemini's 'Organize' acts only when the user asks, and API push notifications are developer building blocks, so neither counts as autonomous automation. Missing for 10: AI-driven background agents, user-configurable recurring or scheduled automations beyond simple filter rules, multi-step workflows, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: When a message matches, filters automatically trigger actions such as adding or removing labels, or forwarding the email to a specified address.
Advanced rules configured for an account that evaluate incoming messages against specific matching criteria (like sender, subject, or size).
After you search, you can use the results to set up a filter for these messages.
